_comment: Treasure by the Dungeon Master's Guide (2024), chapters 4 and 7 (game/treasure.py). Money is in gold pieces here (x100 copper in the game). individual: [CR from, CR to, dice, times, coin] for what one creature carries. hoard: [CR from, CR to, dice, times (GP), magic items] for a hoard (CR 11-16: the book prints 8d8 x 10,000 with an average of 36,000, more than the CR 17+ row; the average is kept, so x 1,000). rarity: the Magic Item Rarities table by level band, used with the hoard's CR (enemies scale with the land, not the party): [from, to, [top roll for common, uncommon, rare, very rare]], legendary above. themes: what monetary treasure each theme turns into. gems and art: values in GP and the names of the stones and things (the art in the game's own words). bars and goods: [item, GP]. tables: the random magic item tables by theme and rarity, [from, to, codex slug, variant]; makers say how the game makes the items it has so far, and anything else is rolled again, so treasure grows with each expansion. reroll: how many tries before a Realmwalker item of the same rarity and theme is made instead. magic_scale: magic items found, by the world's Magic setting (1 scarce, 2, 3).

props.text: Reinforced with adamantine: a critical hit against the wearer is only a hit.
Adamantine: every hit on a thing (a door, a chest, a barricade) is a critical hit.
Mithral, light and supple: no Strength needed, no clatter to give you away, and it can be worn under clothes.
Silvered: a critical hit on a shapechanger deals one more die of damage.
A bonus action coats the blade with venom once a day: the next hit within a minute, DC 15 Constitution save or 2d10 poison damage and Poisoned for a minute.
While worn: immune to poison damage and to being Poisoned.
Every hit does 2d6 more damage of the weapon's own kind.
A humanoid it hits takes 2d6 slashing damage more, and you gain as many temporary hit points.
A hit does 2d6 necrotic damage more, and a Constitution save (DC 15) or the one struck cannot regain hit points (a save at the end of each of its turns ends it).
A 20 on the die: 14 slashing damage more and a level of exhaustion. A thing struck takes the most the dice can give.
It cuts through resistance to slashing. A 20 on the die takes off the head of a creature that cannot live without it; others take 30 slashing damage more.
Hurt by a creature within reach: the reaction strikes back at it, with Advantage, and nothing resists the blow.

curse.text: A vengeful spirit lives in the blade: bound to it, you will not part with it, other weapons turn in your hand, and whoever hurts you must pay.

props.text: Disadvantage with any other weapon; hurt by a foe, a Wisdom save (DC 15) or every blow goes at that foe until one of you falls.
One blow with it as a bonus action on each of your turns.
A bonus action tosses it into the air: it flies 30 feet and strikes with your blow, again with each bonus action, and comes back to your hand after the fourth.
As each of your turns begins, some of the +3 may go to your Armor Class until the next (the battle's judgement: more when you are pressed).
Luck: once a day a failed save or a missed blow is rolled again, and the second roll stands.
Wish, from its charges, once a day; spent charges never come back.
The Magic action spends a charge on a wave of terror: foes within 30 feet make a Wisdom save (DC 15) or run from you for a minute (1d3 charges back at dawn).
Its buttons make it a flaming blade (2d6 fire damage more), an axe or a spear, and the mace again, each with a bonus action.
Drain Life, once a day on a hit: a Constitution save (DC 17) or 4d6 necrotic damage more, and you regain half of it.
Paralyze, once a day on a hit: a Constitution save (DC 17) or Paralyzed for a minute (a save at the end of each turn).
Terrify, once a day: foes within 30 feet make a Wisdom save (DC 17) or are frightened for a minute.
A battering ram: +10 to force a stuck or barred door.
It points to the north: +5 to keep your bearings.
A walking cane (it strikes as a club) or a longsword, changed with a bonus action.
You and your friends within 30 feet roll Initiative with Advantage, and it wakes your camp when danger comes in the night.
+5 to Sleight of Hand.
Nobody can see or feel them on your hands: no search or robber finds them.
They leave the tracks of other people: a band of people trailing you reads them wrong, and you see them first more often.
